thread.title: Tech Today: Apple at $1 Trillion Soon, IAC Surges, Cheers for Arista

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Apple at $1 Trillion Soon, IAC Surges, Cheers for Arista
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated May 10, 2018 12:06 p.m. ET Roku CEO Anthony Wood on CNBC May 10th, 2018. Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Apple's $1 Trillion Market Cap Coming Right Up
Everyone’s been fixated of late on Apple’s ( AAPL ) proximity to an historic $1 trillion dollar market cap, given it currently trades at $958 billion, given a current price of $189.04 with 5.068 billion shares outstanding.
One analyst thinks it can be soon .
M onness Crespi Hardt ’s Brian White blames the stock multiple for Apple not already being there: the price-earnings multiple of just 12.2 times next year’s projected earnings for Apple should be much higher, he believes.
Writes White, "Given Apple’s strong earnings results last week with a return to iPhone unit growth driven by the iPhone X, combined with a strong performance delivered in Greater China and meaningful upside in the Services business, we believe Apple is on a path to surpass the $1 trillion market-capitalization milestone in the coming months .”
"If Apple traded at the average P/E multiple (17x CY19) of consumer-related stocks” such as Coca Cola ( KO ), writes White, "Apple would already have a market capitalization north of $1 trillion."
Apple needs to hit $197.32 in share price to reach $1 trillion.
In other Apple news, CNBC’s Josh Lipton reported a short while ago Apple is partnering with Goldman Sachs Group (GS) to introduce a joint credit card .
Broadcom Cut Again
Shares of chip giant Broadcom ( AVGO ) are up $3.25, or 1.4%, at $241.30, despite the stock getting another cut in price target today.
Thomas Diffely of D.A. Davidson cuts his target to $300 from $325, while maintaining his Buy rating. This follows one from Bernstein yesterday .
Diffely is trimming his estimates for Broadcom as the smartphone market is "now experiencing a period of inventory correction."
Diffely expects earnings per share in the July-ending fiscal Q3 will come in lower than previously expected, at $4.52 versus $4.78, but he keeps his revenue estimate at $5.05 billion. But revenue should rebound in the latter half of the year, as the “long-term drivers remain in place,” such as 5G wireless networking.
Roku’s Kudos
Shares of Roku ( ROKU ) are up 22 cents, or 0.6%, at $36.30, after its Q1 revenue and profit topped consensus yesterday afternoon and the outlook for this quarter’s revenue beat as well.
Price targets are rising at some shops. KeyBanc ’s Evan Wingren reiterates an Overweight rating, and raises his price target to $44 from $42, writing that he sees "proof points that Roku's competitive position in streaming is strengthening."
Even bears are impressed: Tom Forte with D.A. Davidson reiterates a Neutral rating, while raising his price target to $32 from $30, calling the report “impressive,” and titling his note "Really Outstanding KUdos!
IAC Rising
Interactive media holding company IAC/InterActiveCorp ( IAC ) is another winner from yesterday, up up $5.95, or 4.3%, at $144.71, after beating expectations and raising its 2018 profit outlook.
Evercore ISI ’s Anthony DiClemente writes "we believe investors come away pleased” with results from the company’s two major properties, Match Group ( MTCH ) and Angi Homeservices ( ANGI ).
He notes, too, that "trends at the ‘stub', particularly Publishing and Video, continue to inflect positively."
However, Piper Jaffray ’s Sam Kemp cut his target on the stock to $200 from $218 despite reiterating an Overweight rating, to account for the “conglomerate discount.” That will no doubt be rather annoying to CEO Joey Levin , who has repeatedly said the stock doesn’t deserve such as discount. See last night’s comments to Barron’s by Levin .
Another Qualcomm Repurchase Still to Come
Shares of Qualcomm ( QCOM ) are up $1.43, or 2.7%, at $54.60, after the company last night announced its board of directors authorized a new share repurchase authorization of $10 billion to replenish a prior $15 billion allotment that has been all but exhausted, with $1.2 billion remaining.
Raymond James’s Chris Caso, who has an Outperform rating on the shares, this morning writes that he spoke to the company and confirmed that this buyback plan is "is separate from the $25-30 billion buyback the company mentioned on the last earnings call, which would be effected in the event the NXP acquisition did not close,” referring to ” referring to Qualcomm's pending acquisition of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), which the company has been working on since October 2016 .
"In the event NXP doesn’t close, there would be a new authorization issued for that buyback."
Arista’s Bright Prospects
Shares of networking-technology vendor Arista Networks ( ANET ) are up $2.06, or 0.8%, at $261.48, after Credit Suisse ’s Sami Badri this morning initiated coverage of the stock with an Outperform rating, and a $303 price target, after concluding in a companion report that " cloud networking " is going to increasing take over parts of the market, referring to the kind of equipment sold for very large Internet data centers.
"We believe the future of networking lies in the cloud networking fabric providers,” writes Badri, adding, "Arista Networks comes out on top, as it is the best-in-class cloud networking fabric vendor given its elastic and versatile EOS solution."
Badri’s top pick, however, is not Arista but rather F5 Networks ( FFIV ), which he deems “highly leveraged to benefit from hybrid cloud transitions,” as its technology is "necessary in helping their customers shift their IT workloads into the cloud."
F5 shares are up $1.63, or 1%, at $173.63.
Trade Desk, Nvidia on Tap
Shares of Trade Desk ( TTD ), the online advertising technology provider that went public in late September, are up $1.98, or almost 4%, at $53.50, after Oppenheimer & Co .’s Brian Schwartz initiated coverage of the stock late yesterday, ahead of Trade Desk’s earnings report this afternoon, after the closing bell.
Schwartz assigned an Outperform rating, and a $66 price target, writing that the company is "in front of a very large established market that's on the cusp of converging with the large customer relationship market.” Schwartz thinks the "convergence should spotlight TTD as a unique SaaS asset and catalyze a higher valuation."
"Additionally, if management embarked on a strategy to increase revenue predictability through fixed fees with agencies it would likely increase valuation."
Other earnings reports this afternoon include Nvidia ( NVDA ), Dropbox ( DROP ), Amber Road ( AMBR ), Amdocs ( DOX ), Avid Technology ( AVID ), Hubspot ( HUBS ), Talend ( TLND ), and Yelp ( YELP ).
